start.note: Day 107: the winter's first days. The stay port's folk notice, once.

start.text: Oda's taken you on. Coil sun-wise, or she'll have you off at the breakwater and you'll swim it.
Walking, Oda says. You'll come back past the dock, then. Everybody does.
Boats out past the wall again. I count them in of an evening by the Spire's light. Harbormaster's never had it so easy, and I don't trust it.
start.note: Day 98: Mara after the homecoming, per ending.

start.text: Tam's taken a blanket up to the Gull. For the step, he says. I've not asked who it's for. I've let him.
The list's on the dock-post under the lantern. Three names on it so far, and every one of them put there by its own hand. Mine's not one. Yet.
Aldous went down the dock with his bag and got on the Mercy. Didn't say where. Left the bottle on the bench, stood up and corked. Tam walks round it like it's a dog asleep.
start.note: Day 113: Mara noticing Aldous gone to Kindleby.

start.text: Oda says Aldous is keeping a door on Kindleby for the Keepers. Sober, she says. I've left the bottle where it is. If he wants it he can come and ask me for it.
He came back with leave, he says, and sits there with the bottle beside him, corked. He told me I'd say he wasn't gone long enough to be missed. So I didn't say it.

first.text: Stop there. Let me see your hand.
She looks at the ember a long moment. Her jaw works like she's chewing something bitter.
Mara Tollen. Harbormaster. These days that means I count what's left and try not to count what isn't.
If you're what the old songs say, you picked a fine time to wash up.

choice.text: What happened here?
"What isn't" — who's missing?
Someone in the net-lofts saw Dunstan leave.
How do we push the fog back?
Where do I find the Keeper?
Listen to this. It hums.
Pell has the humming pebble now.
The beacon needs a memory. It could be yours — of Dunstan.
Your gull. The beacon didn't need it.
There's grey lying out past the harbor mouth.
choice.note: Day 120: the offshore bank (Day 119) before the burn.

choice.text: The grey off the harbor mouth has drawn back.
choice.note: Day 120: the bank leaned back after the burn, per burn.

choice.text: The bank off the harbor mouth.
choice.note: Day 120: the bank after the homecoming, per ending (lit thins it: game.json after_the_ember).

choice.text: Aldous says the ferry might run again.
Show Mara the Keeper's sleeve-ember.
The ferry's in.
About Pell and the ferry.
Dunstan sent you this.
Brenner kept a tally of Dunstan's dare. To the Low Water's edge.
Brenner says the dare went to the Low Water's edge. Not the bank.
I'll be going.

what_happened.text: Three months back the Hearthspire went dark. The Snuffing, folk call it, like naming it makes it smaller.
The fog came in behind it. First the net-lofts. Then the smokehouse. People go in to fetch a net and come out not knowing whose net it is.

dunstan.text: My brother. Dunstan. Two weeks ago he walked north into the grey with a lantern and no reason he'd give me.
He's not dead. I'd know. I'd— I think I'd know.

beacon_offer.text: The Gull's Beacon, up on the headland. Every midwinter the Keepers lit it from the Spire, and the fog kept its distance.
There's a Keeper in the village. Brother Aldous. Came off the Spire the night it went out and hasn't been sober since.

choice.text: I'll talk to him.
Why haven't you asked him yourself?

why_not.text: I have. He cries. Maybe he'll talk to someone with fire in their hand.

token.text: Take this. It'll get you past the lads at the net-lofts when the time comes.

where_aldous.text: West side, by the Wrens' old house. Follow the smell of cheap spirits.

pebble_kept.text: When the hum reaches her, Mara's eyes go wet. She hums three notes along with it, stops, frowns.
I knew the rest of that. Yesterday I knew it. Keep it safe, Wakebearer.

pebble_given.text: Pell showed me. Carries it everywhere and hums along all day now. Wrong, mind you, but hums it.
Good of you. That child's got precious little that's their own.

dunstan_chose.text: Hesk? Hesk's been Hushed a month. She doesn't know her own—
You tell her: the lantern, the laughing, coming back for his name.
…That's him. That's exactly him, the great fool.
So the fog didn't take him. He went. He walked in there on purpose and didn't tell me why.
I don't know if that's better. Ask me when I've slept.

offer_gull.text: You're asking me to forget my brother.
…He chose, didn't he. Walked off laughing and left me the counting. Maybe I get a choice too.
He's out there. If I forget him, who's left to be waiting when he comes back?

choice.text: Only if you're willing. It has to be your choice.
Forget I asked.

offer_gull_yes.text: She takes something from her coat: a thumb-sized gull whittled from driftwood, its beak worn smooth by a thumb.
He made it for me when I was six and he was ten. Wouldn't let me on the boats, so he brought me a bird.
She walks to the boardwalk gate and holds the gull out into the grey. She stays there a long time. When she comes back the wood is warm, and her eyes are wet and angry.
There. It's all in there. Don't— don't tell me if you use it. I won't know what you mean anyway.

gull_back.text: Mara turns the gull over in her fingers. The warmth fades out of it as you watch, back into her.
Great fool of a bird. Great fool of a brother.
Thank you. I mean it. Now go away before I say something soft.

beacon_lit.text: I watched it catch from the harbor wall. Half the village did. Old Brenner dropped his pipe in the water.
The fog's back past the wall. We can reach the smokehouse again. The lofts, even. You've fed us for the winter, Wakebearer.

lit_pebble.text: She hums, absently — three notes, four — and stops. She frowns at the air.
Was I humming? Odd. I don't know any songs. Never had the voice for it.

lit_knot.text: Strange thing. I went to show Tam how to start a new net and my hands didn't know where to begin. Started from the middle. Works fine.
Suppose that's what it cost. A beginning. We'll manage without one.

lit_gull.text: She glances at the empty stool beside her door, the one with a big man's dent worn into the seat, and looks away without seeing it.
Just me here. Tollens end with me, always have. Never minded.
…Though I keep setting out two cups. Habit, I suppose. Whose, I couldn't tell you.

ferry.text: Does he. Well. He's not wrong, for once.
He told you something, then. You've the look of someone carrying a Keeper's secret. Don't hand it to me; I've enough to carry.
The Tidewright ferry puts in at our dock when it can see us. It hasn't since the Snuffing. No ferryman sails into what they can't see, and I don't blame them.
Now there's a light on the Gull, they'll see it from the lanes. I'll hang the green lantern on the post outside my door. Old harbor signal: passengers waiting.
When they come, you'll hear the horn. Might be days. Might be longer. The sea doesn't hurry for anyone, even you.

sleeve_ember.text: Mara turns the scrap of robe to the light. The stitched ember on it has faded almost to pink.
That's off a Keeper's sleeve. They're buried in those robes, sleeves and all. He cut it off himself?
Then whatever he told you, he meant it. First thing Aldous Wren's meant since he washed up here.
Keep it out of sight on the ferry. Tidewrights don't love Keepers. They'll say the Spire went dark on the Keepers' watch, and they won't be wrong.

farewell.text: Heard it. Whole village heard it. Hesk'll have heard it up in the lofts, if she hears anything now.
Funny thing. I set out two cups this morning, same as always, and I thought: one of those is for a traveller. That'll be you, then. Drink it before you go. It's cold.
There's a tune I've been after all morning. Something to send a boat off with. Can't find it. Never mind; the horn'll do.
Tidewrights'll give you grief about the knot. Let them. The nets still hold. That's what nets are for.

farewell_dunstan.text: And— if you see a big man out there in the fog. Tollen shoulders. Laughs like a dropped anchor.
Tell him the stool's still by the door. Don't tell him to come home. He knows where it is.

farewell_end.text: Go on, then. Light the next one. And eat something before you board; Tidewright cooking is a punishment.

pell_ferry.text: Pell's told me nothing, which is how I know something's up. That bundle's got my good cup in it.
You promised a child a crossing into the fog. Without asking me.
The kid gave up that pebble for this village. Doesn't even know what they gave. Maybe that's earned a bit of sea.

choice.text: I'll keep Pell close. You have my word, on the ember.
You're right. Pell should stay with you.

pell_ferry_yes.text: Mara looks down the dock for a long while. Pell is pretending very hard not to watch.
Pell's not mine to keep. Never was. Nobody I love ever is, it seems.
…Odd. I feel I've said that before, about someone. Can't think who.
Go on, tell the kid before I change my mind. And you bring them back with all their fingers.

pell_ferry_no.text: Then you tell the kid. You made the promise. You unmake it.
She says it without heat, and it lands harder for that.

gull_from_dunstan.text: Mara takes the little gull and turns it over in her square fingers, the way you'd check a knot somebody else tied.
He said to set it on the stool, facing the door. And that it's not a promise. Only so you'd know he knows where it is.
Course it's not a promise. Great fool never made one in his life he didn't laugh his way out of.
She sets it on the dented seat, beak to the door, and stands looking at it a while with her arms folded.
There. When he comes, it'll be the first thing he sees. If he comes.

dunstan_home.text: He came in backward. Course he did. Rowed the whole lane facing the wrong way, lantern in the stern, laughing at nothing, and half the harbor on the wall to see.
I didn't go down. Somebody had to set the stool square.
She folds her arms and looks at the harbor, not at him, and not at you.
You walked him in. He told me. Don't make anything of it, and don't let him.

stranger_home.text: There's a big man on the stool by my door. Came in backward in a rowboat with a lantern in the stern, and sat down there like he'd paid for it.
Says he's my brother. I've no reason on earth to believe it. Tollens end with me.
She looks at the two cups on the crate. For once, they're both drained.
But the second cup's his. I knew that the minute he picked it up. Don't ask me how. I'll not have it asked.

winter_stay.text: Oda came up the dock to tell me you're wintering here. Thirty-eight years she's never once walked up my dock to tell me anything, so I knew it mattered to her.
There's the loft over the net store. Dry, mostly. The gulls only walk on it of a morning.
You'll see the Spire from the loft hatch. I've put the bed so you can look at it from the pillow, or not, as you like. Turn it round if you'd rather.
Tam'll want you up the Gull with him some nights, for the step. Say no if you like. He'll go anyway.
You'll want to know: you're not on the list on the dock-post, and nobody'd let you put yourself there. You've given enough. Harbormaster's word.

choice.text: Thank you, Mara.
I'll pay my way.

winter_thanks.text: Don't. You woke on our shingle. That makes you somebody's, and it may as well be ours.

winter_pay.text: You'll mend nets like the rest of us. Badly, the first month.

bank.text: The Greying. Came in off the sea the week after the Snuffing and lay down out there like it had found a mooring.
Nobody takes a boat past the outer post now. Brenner went out for the cod grounds once. Came back with his nets full and couldn't tell me what they were for.
Every other island's on the far side of that. The lanes run through it. That's why there's been no ferry, and why there won't be, while the Gull's dark.

bank_back.text: You asked me about that, before. Look at it now.
Leaned back off the mouth like a dog from a fire. Tam paced it from the outer post with an oar: four boat-lengths, and thinner. You can see the swell through it of a morning.
Brenner's on about the cod grounds again. I've told him the Gull reaches so far and no farther. He'll go anyway. Somebody always does.
Something ought to be sung about it, a thing that size going back. Can't think what. Never had the voice anyway.
Tam says it lies out there like a net with nobody hauling. He's been saying things like that since the lofts came back. I let him.

bank_back_gull.text: She looks at the edge of it a long while, out past the post, where the swell goes pale.
Somebody used to row out to the edge of that and back, for a dare. Every spring, the first calm day. I can see the boat plain as I see you.
Can't see who's in it. Odd. Must have been before my time.

bank_after.text: Gone to a haze. Some mornings you can't find it at all. Brenner's out on the cod grounds every day the tide gives him, and he comes back knowing what his nets are for.
I still go down to the outer post of a morning to look where it lay. Habit. Harbormaster's habit is counting what isn't there.
Still out there, just where the Gull leaned it. No thicker, no thinner. Tam says it's waiting to see what the step's for.
I say it's fog. But I don't row out to it, and neither does he.
Same as the day you left. The Gull holds it off the mouth and that's all the light we've got until midwinter.
Whoever's name goes first on that list, that's what they'll be pushing back. I make every one of them stand at the post and look at it before they write.

dare.text: For a moment she looks about fourteen, and cross about it.
I knew. Every spring, the first calm day, I'd be down at the outer post with my arms folded, so he'd see I wasn't watching. Twenty-two springs.
Brenner thinks I never knew. Let him. You don't take the count off a man who's kept it.
And you've got it in your pocket. Taking it to him? Don't tell him I knew. Let him have that one.
He sat on Brenner's box and had the old man cut a twenty-third. I watched from the post. Arms folded.

dare_gull.text: She turns from the harbor mouth to the south, past the Gull, where the skerries go out pale toward the singing.
That's right. The bank wasn't there, then. I'd put the boat where the grey is, because the grey's what I look at now.
I can see it better for being told. Further out, oars shipped, sun on the water, and them sat so still to listen. Then turning her round. They always turned round.
Brenner showed me his stick. Twenty-two. I keep meaning to ask him who for, and then not.
Brenner says you've his stick now. Mind it. It's the only count there is.
The big fellow on the stool laughed when I told him that, and spilled his cup. Wouldn't say why. Then he went up the breakwater to sit with Brenner.
